Issued at 242 AM MDT Sun Oct 11 2026

It still looks like a rather active several days across the area. 
And like last night, we have some things we are fairly high 
confidence in and others that have more uncertainty. We will go over 
these below, that is why you read the discussion, of course.

Areas of showers are moving across portions of the state as I write 
this after midnight, with the greatest concentration of them largely 
across the northern half of the state. These will continue through 
the night as cold air over runs a cold front that has now slid down 
to around the Continental Divide (it went through Riverton not long 
ago, our wind switched to the north and the temperature dropped 
around 10 degrees). We will continue to showers on and off through 
the day, with the best coverage once again across western Wyoming. 
Overall, coverage of showers still looks to be the greatest today as 
we see the maximum impacts of the moisture streaming northward from 
the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel. Overall reasoning looks 
similar to yesterday, with most numerous showers likely later today 
and into tonight as the deepest moisture moves toward the area. The 
deepest moisture still looks to remain west of Wyoming over eastern 
Idaho, but it will get close to the area. We continue to have a 
marginal risk of excessive rainfall across the area, this looks 
reasonable as there will be locally heavy rainfall. And, we have 
another concern this morning. Some subsidence with a possibly dry 
slot may develop from Sweetwater through Casper. Most models are 
showing 50 to 60 knots of wind at 700 millibars. The NBM ensemble 
gives a greater than 1 out of 2 chance of wind gusts past 55 mph 
across this area as well. With this we have hoisted a high wind 
watch from eastern Sweetwater County through Natrona County, 
although the best chance of high wind in Natrona County would be in 
western Natrona, not near Casper. Wind should decrease as the 
subsidence decreases toward sunrise. And, there will likely be some 
snow in the higher elevations, I will discuss this later in the 
discussion as well as rainfall amounts.

As we head into Monday, this looks to be a bit of a lull as the 
deeper moisture from Rachel moves away to the north and east. This 
is when the dominant feature becomes an upper level low that will 
move out of the Pacific northwest and into the Great Basin. This is 
where the uncertainty begins to increase. Some deterministic models 
as well as some ensemble members keep the low further south, 
dropping it further south toward southern Utah as well as Colorado. 
This would keep the greatest forcing and moisture further south, and 
any showers largely confined to southern Wyoming. The European and 
some other ensemble members are further north, taking the upper level 
low closer to the Wyoming-Colorado border which would spread better 
chances of showers further northward. The current forecast is 
somewhere in the middle, keeping most showers West of the Divide 
through day, then pushing deeper moisture further northward on 
Monday night This will be a cool day as well, with below normal 
temperatures across most of the area. 

Tuesday looks similar, as we may be somewhat of a lull in the 
showers, with most activity confined to southern Wyoming. By Tuesday 
night, details become more uncertain. Like yesterday, the GFS 
remains the faster model, with the low being moved to the east, with 
all precipitation ending by Wednesday night. The European and some 
other ensemble members continue to show the upper level low cutting 
off the upper level low and keeping unsettled weather around through 
most of the week. There will likely (greater than a 2 out of 3 
chance) of an area of steady precipitation across central Wyoming as 
a period of east to northeasterly upslope flow develops. There are 
still differences on exactly when this will occur (anytime from 
Tuesday night through Wednesday night) and the exact position of the 
heaviest precipitation. The chance is definitely there though. Some, 
we continue to be confident of a cooler and unsettled pattern. 
However, confidence in the details remains rather low, especially 
from Tuesday and beyond.

PRECIPITATION AMOUNTS...I will divide this into two periods. This 
first through tonight with the moisture from Rachel, and then in the 
period following that. Most ensemble guidance continues to show the 
heaviest rain across the western mountains and higher elevations, 
with lesser amounts further south and east. The area generally north 
and west of a Kemmerer to Buffalo line has at least a 1 out of 2 
chance of a quarter inch of QPF or more, with most falling this 
afternoon and evening. The chance of an inch or more is largely
